_meta: iter 79: curated complexity-claim drills for Smell-test mode. Each entry pairs a lesson with its actual time complexity + a plausible-but-wrong distractor. The session randomly shows actual OR distractor as the 'claim'; user picks correct/wrong + sees the actual either way. Trains the interview reflex 'does the stated complexity match the code?' — graded heavily but never trained in isolation.

two-sum.note: Single pass with a hash map; complement check is O(1) amortized.

valid-palindrome.note: Two pointers walk the string once; alphanumeric filter is per-char O(1).

p-bfs.note: Each node enqueued once, processed once.

binary-search.note: Each iteration halves the search space.

p-3sum.note: Sort is O(n log n); the outer loop × inner two-pointer pass is O(n²).

p-merge-intervals.note: Sort dominates; the merge pass after sorting is O(n).

p-min-window.note: Each character entered and exited the window at most once; amortized linear.

valid-parentheses.note: Single pass over the string with O(1) stack push/pop per char.

p-contains-dup.note: Hash-set seen-check is O(1) amortized; single linear pass.

p-anagrams.note: Sort each of n words of length k as the hash key; map ops are O(1) amortized.

p-reverse-list.note: Single pass swapping next-pointers; each node touched exactly once.

p-cycle.note: Floyd's tortoise/hare — fast pointer catches slow in linear steps.

p-merge-two-sorted.note: Single walk advancing whichever list has the smaller head; each node enqueued once.

p-invert.note: Visits every node once to swap children — O(n), not O(log n) (height-only bounds don't apply when you touch every node).

p-max-depth.note: Recursion visits every node to compute the depth — linear, not log (log n applies only to balanced search, not full traversal).

p-same-tree.note: Pairwise pre-order traversal; each pair of nodes compared once.

p-islands.note: Each cell DFS-visited at most once across all island-starts (sink-in-place via the visited mark).

p-num-provinces.note: Union-find over the n × n adjacency matrix — every cell visited; near-linear in n² with path compression.

p-permutations.note: n! permutations × O(n) work per permutation to copy/track choices — not 2ⁿ (that's subsets).

p-subsets.note: 2ⁿ subsets × O(n) work per subset to copy — not n! (that's permutations).

p-trapping-rain.note: Two-pointer pass tracking max-left/max-right walls — single linear sweep, no nested loop.

p-coin-change.note: DP table fills in amount rows × coins columns — the coin count is the multiplier, not amount itself.

p-top-k-frequent.note: Min-heap of size k — n inserts each log k, not log n (heap is bounded at k).

p-kth-largest.note: Min-heap of size k — log k per insert, not amortized O(1) (heap insert is logarithmic).

p-clone-graph.note: DFS/BFS visiting every node once and every edge once — graph-traversal standard.

p-climbing-stairs.note: Bottom-up DP (or 2-variable iteration) is O(n). The O(2^n) is the NAIVE recursion without memoization — the trap candidates fall into when they describe the recursion before the iterative answer.

best-time-stock.note: Single pass tracking min-so-far + best profit. The O(n²) is the brute-force pair-loop that most interview candidates name first before catching the linear refinement.

p-house-robber.note: 1D DP (or rolling two variables) — each house is visited once. The O(2^n) is the naive 'pick or skip' recursion without memo — same trap shape as Climbing Stairs.

p-koko-bananas.note: Binary search on the speed-answer space (1 to max pile = m), each candidate speed checked in O(n) over piles. The O(n × m) is the linear-scan-all-speeds brute force.

p-jump-game.note: Greedy single-pass tracking max-reachable index. Often misclassified as DP (which would be O(n²) — for each index, scan all reachable next positions).

p-lru-cache.note: Doubly-linked list + hash map keys → constant-time get + put. The O(n) is naive Array.shift / splice-based implementations.

p-meeting-rooms-ii.note: Sort by start time + min-heap of end times (or two-pointer on sorted starts + ends). The O(n²) is the brute-force pair-overlap check.

p-max-subarray.note: Kadane's algorithm — single pass tracking current-sum vs reset. The O(n²) is the brute-force sum-every-subarray which every candidate names before remembering Kadane.
